props.title: Jahmyr Gibbs OVER 29.5 receiving yards
props.cutoff: OVER 29.5 at -115 or better only; pass at 30.5+ or -116 and worse. Reverify the live price after expiry.
props.edge: Projected mean +3.5 yards, not a probability edge. Uncalibrated judgment: about 55% to clear, versus 53.49% break-even at -115 (about +1.5 percentage points; about +2.8% expected return if that estimate is right). Plausible 50–60% uncertainty includes negative value.
props.why: The verified 29.5-yard number is below his 34.4 last-five and 44.9 last-ten averages. Five targets and 30 receiving yards in Week 1 support continuing receiving involvement; the team confirms an expanded lead-back role. My conservative 33-yard projection uses 5.5 targets × 75% catches × 8 yards per catch, below the recent target averages. Buffalo favored by 5.5 gives a plausible passing script. Detroit line absences may encourage outlets, but that is an inference, not the main reason.
props.risk: Thin estimated edge and uncertain routes under a new coordinator. Missing Mahogany and Miller could require Gibbs to block instead. Buffalo held Houston RBs to four catches for 17 yards last week; that one game does not prove a favorable matchup. Overtime inflated Week 1 touches. Inactives and wind remain pregame checks; no unsupported weather or scheme boost.

parlays.why: This exact four-leg package was directly offered in DraftKings’ Indiana experience at +360. The 60-yard Cook and 25-yard Gibbs alternatives are below the researched full-game means; the tight ends need four catches rather than five. At these exact thresholds, last-five/last-ten hits are Cook 3/5 and 6/10, Gibbs 3/5 and 7/10, Kincaid 2/5 and 4/10, LaPorta 4/5 and 7/10. This is an optional speculative fun selection, not a core favorite. Research confidence 6/10 describes verified quote, rules and supporting data, not a 60% chance of winning.
parlays.risk: Kincaid four catches is the weakest historical leg; his five-catch opener does not prove a stable new role. Cook had only 13 carries for 57 yards last week. His two-carry Week 18 rest game stays in the sample. Detroit’s two missing offensive-line starters may reduce route opportunities. All four legs must win; normal workload can still miss one. Official inactives were not yet released/verified at this review.
parlays.edge: No demonstrated positive EV and no calibrated joint probability. +360 requires 21.74% to break even; no claim is made that this ticket exceeds that. It returns +3.6u profit and 4.6u total only if every leg wins at the recorded price. Individual historical rates are not multiplied. This is deliberately separate from favorites and their returns.
parlays.correlation: All legs share one game’s pace and script. Cook rushing can trade off with Buffalo passing volume. Gibbs and LaPorta compete for Detroit targets. These dependencies can help or hurt; +360 is the actual offered combined sportsbook price, never a product of single-leg odds. It also repeats exposure to the earlier Gibbs and LaPorta straight selections; this is intentional entertainment overlap, not diversification.

takeaways: Sep 17, 17:34 ET: Gibbs receiving yards rose 29.5 to 31.5 at DraftKings. LaPorta stayed 4.5 catches while its over price shortened +116 to +101. The reasons for those moves are unknown.

Sep 17 evening review: two Detroit offensive-line starters are out. Borom and Bartch are likely replacements, not confirmed starters. Extra blocking for backs/tight ends is a risk, not a verified role change.
NWS Orchard Park forecast updated 15:57 ET: about 68°F and NW 5 mph near kickoff, light precipitation risk. No material passing-weather penalty was added.

Means are not hit probabilities. LaPorta projections ranging 4.2–4.8 cannot by themselves validate the earlier 53% over estimate. Preserve and evaluate that original call rather than rewrite its result.

The +360 fun ticket uses true alternate thresholds. LaPorta 4+ receptions hit 7/10 prior played games; OVER 4.5 hit 6/10. Thresholds must match before a hit rate is displayed. Kincaid 4+ is only 4/10, so this ticket is high risk despite its lower yardage alternatives.
